items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.7 registers ELDER_GUARDIAN (SimpleParticleType, wire id 16, overrideLimiter=true) with a MobAppearanceParticle$Provider (ParticleEngine.registerProviders, javap offset 281) and spawns it on game event 10. The port's ParticleType enum (127 variants) lacks it, so received_particle drops server-sent elder_guardian packets, /particle rejects it (particle.notFound), and the providers driver cannot pass its 12 elder_guardian cases (probe prints 'no provider'). The in-game curse apparition IS re-implemented via game event 10 + elder_apparition_geometry (30-tick lifetime), so the main visible path works through a different mechanism (fidelity unverified).
items.title: elder_guardian has no port implementation at all: no ParticleType variant, no engine provider, no limiter entry

items.evidence: Particle::read decodes wire id 41 (flash) as Color(i32) — a flash particle always carries a colour — but hub_particle has no Flash arm in its Color match, so the packet is built with data None and Particle::write (writes data by presence, not id) emits the id with no colour bytes; guests reading id 41 consume the next 4 stream bytes as the colour and desync. Reachable only via /particle flash on a LAN host (Flash is otherwise created client-side only, in firework explosions); the local player draws directly and is unaffected.
items.title: /particle minecraft:flash sends a malformed packet to LAN guests

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.7 registers SPRUCE_LEAVES as TintedParticleLeavesBlock with leafParticleChance 0.01 (Blocks.class BootstrapMethods -> lambda$static$36 -> TintedParticleLeavesBlock(0.01F); LeavesBlock.animateTick rolls nextFloat() < chance). The port maps spruce_leaves to Animate::Leaves(None, None, false) — no falling particle. All 10 other leaf blocks match vanilla (cherry 0.1, pale oak 0.02, rest tinted 0.01; azalea fixed colour -9399763 matches exactly). The marker driver would fail its spruce zoo cases (oracle emits, probe emits none); the driver's own comment ('the spruce that never falls') encodes the same wrong belief and needs correcting with the fix.
items.title: Spruce leaves never drop falling-leaf particles

method: Static analysis only (no driver runs, no cargo tests — blocked). javap -c on the named 1.21.7 client jar (stream3-e6-quick/jars/1.21.7-client-named.jar) and server jar (leakage-audit/jars/1.21.7-server-named.jar); direct class-file parsing of Blocks.class (constant pool + BootstrapMethods + bytecode scans) for the leaves association, where javap was too slow under CPU throttle; source comparison against versions/1.21.7/crates/; data diffs against mob-spawn/resources registries.json (jar-verified: ParticleTypes <clinit> order == protocol_id for all 114). Registry/type coverage, wire-codec ids, override-limiter flags, entity-burst table, marker-zoo coverage, leaves chances, dripstone/tag checks, oracle API existence, and oracle-compile evidence from the previous agent's run log (.local/parity-runner/logs/item_particles.log).

Scope: all 114 particle types, emitters, providers; 8 drivers found in the tree (7 particle-named + effect_sync, particle-adjacent; the plan claims 9, the 9th is unaccounted for). Second re-spawn: the previous agent's setup commits c1f1428a (six oracle repairs) and 4259cdb9 (driver/probe adaptation) were verified intact and are already on origin/parity-sweep.
systemic_note: No single systemic root cause like the pilot's tag pattern: the three defects are three different shapes — a missing registry entry carried through every table (B8-G01: one type absent from the enum, the limiter list, the command parser and the probe), a write-path/read-path asymmetry in one codec arm (B8-G02: the reader expects data the writer omits), and a wrong per-block belief baked into both the port and the driver's own comment (B8-G03: spruce). The positive systemic finding is that the port's particle tables are otherwise exact: all 114 types covered end-to-end except elder_guardian, all 18 data-carrying wire ids correct, all 28 limiter flags correct except elder_guardian, all 25 entity-burst pairs and all 43 marker-zoo blocks covered, and all 11 leaf blocks' chances verified — the gaps are narrow and enumerated, not a broad drift. The 14 extra 26.x types in the Rust enum (geyser family, poplar leaves, etc.) are dead but unreachable: ids are name-resolved from the server's registry, and a 1.21.7 server never sends those names.
